> Also, how possible would it be for the _joinData to be automatically added from the association's conditions instead of adding it to the data? If a BTM has conditions set with things from the join table, you'd almost always (can't think of when you wouldn't) want those in the joinData when saving. If that could be automatic that'd be awesome.

While possible, I'd rather not add implicit data mutation to the marshaller. I feel that is the kind of behavior that will not be easy to understand at glance.

I've not had a chance to look at the code, but I suspect that all 3 associations using the same `through` table is the source of the persistence issues.

Thanks @markstory. I both at the same time agree and disagree that the `joinData` should be added automatically. I agree because it seems like a magical/dirty thing, but I disagree because it means you always have to do data manipulation when saving a BTM with conditions. How would you suggest doing this automatically in my app if not the core (happy to do that if it's what you suggest)?
When would anyone expect BTM data which is conditional-based to not have those conditions when saving? If the condition isn't there, it won't be there when you do a find after the save, which means the save was pointless. It's definitely a tricky thing..

> How would you suggest doing this automatically in my app if not the core (happy to do that if it's what you suggest)?

You could use one of the event hooks to seed the default data. Both `Model.beforeSave` and `Model.beforeMarshal` are good options.

> why does AssociationCollection::keys return primarytags (sic) for my PrimaryTags association?

Associations are stored in a lowercase form to account for people mistyping associations names.

Using the property name will likely break existing apps using the CamelBacked association names in 'associated' keys. Currently the CamelBacked names are consistently inflected to their lowercase forms. The `associated` key should contain association names, not the property names.

> You'll still have three records in the DB, when you should have one, right? (bug).

It depends on the save strategy for the association.

The 2nd example does seem incorrect to me as well.

I took a look at the [first scenario in your last comment - where primary_tags was replaced](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/7808#issuecomment-165915165), and the current behavior is 'correct'. Because the `_ids` mode does not set any `_joinData` the 3 records set in the first step do not 'match' the association conditions and are not removed when the association links are replaced.

I wasn't able to reproduce the issue you had in the second scenario. I've attached the code I used in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/markstory/c2a10524cc690606041d). As you can see in the SQL log, the last few queries remove the 3 records and replace it with the single tag correctly.

Thanks for the updates on this. I took another look at the code with your updates. And it does seem like something is off. With the StarredTags loaded before marshalling is done, the marshaller does not convert the `_joinData` into an entity and leaves it as an array. Because `_joinData` is not an array it is not persisted which is why we're getting `starred=0`. 

I feel like requiring the `_joinData` association to be marshalled is 'more correct' but the current code makes handling joinData error prone and easy to violate application constraints. I have a good idea on how to fix this now though.
